misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must always be wrapped in if/else statements to be returned as Boolean values.

  lebihBesar : boolean

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrote the solution using a custom comparison approach with bubble sort. In the helper function `is_greater`, they believe they must use if/else to return the boolean result of the comparison `int(str(a) + str(b)) > int(str(b) + str(a))`, when they could simply `return int(str(a) + str(b)) > int(str(b) + str(a))`. The code still works correctly but is unnecessarily verbose. This demonstrates the misconception that conditional expressions must be wrapped in if/else statements to return boolean values, even though the comparison itself already evaluates to a boolean.
